messages:
maria: quick RFC followup — thinking about a lightweight 'softcut' shim between router and rollout controller to normalize canary signals (latency, error-rate, quality probes) and expose a small set of fallback primitives. not trying to replace the whole arbiter, just a compact dialect to reduce miscoordination.

josh: love the name. what's the concrete surface? example config?

maria: minimal API: `ProbeResult{type, value, confidence, window_ms}` + `GraceWindow(ms)` from controller. router consumes normalized events and can decide: continue, throttle, failover.

liam: worried about signal amplification — if downstream adapters double-report we could prematurely flip. how do we dedupe/attenuate?

maria: two parts: 1) attach `source_id` and `seq` to each probe; 2) softcut keeps short-lived sliding window + leaky-bucket smoothing. default attenuation factor 0.5 for noisy sources.

carol: any perf hit on the hot path? even 1% added p99 hurts.

maria: we plan to implement softcut as an opt-in fastpath in the router (in-memory, lock-free), fallback to a sidecar sampler when feature disabled. cost: single atomic append + a small state update per probe. microbenchmarks look <50ns per probe average.

josh: can we see a sample policy snippet?

maria: sure — rough idea:

```yaml
policy:
  id: softcut-default
  probe_types: [latency_ms, grpc_errors, model_ned]
  windows:
    - name: short
      duration_ms: 10000
      threshold: 200
      action: throttle
    - name: degrade
      duration_ms: 60000
      threshold: 150
      action: failover
  smoothing:
    attenuation: 0.5
    dedupe_window_ms: 200
  grace_window_ms: 30000
```

liam: how do rollouts express intent? can the new variant request a different dialect?

maria: controller negotiates dialect at rollout start: `dialect_version` + capability bits (e.g., supports_quality_probe, supports-weighted-evict). router verifies compatibility; incompatible variants get a conservative default.

carol: operations question — when a canary suddenly spikes, ops wants an immediate safe-action (eg drop to 0% and alert). how fast can softcut trigger auto-fallback?

maria: decision latency target is sub-200ms from probe ingestion to route change for short window triggers. we also provide a hard emergency latch: `ops_bypass=true` which instantly routes traffic to fallback and opens an alert in pagerduty.

josh: testing/evangelism: can we run this behind a feature flag and shadow the decisions for 24h?

maria: yes — router can run `dry_run=true` to record intended actions to telemetry without applying them. suggest 24–72h window with aggregated metrics.

carol: telemetry — need clear labels to correlate with traces/spans. what tags?
maria: tagging plan: `rollout_id`, `variant_id`, `dialect_version`, `probe_source`, `decision_action`, `confidence`. also emit raw probe blobs to long-term store for offline analysis.

liam: failure modes — what if softcut crashes or OOMs? we must never make router less reliable.

maria: softcut runs with bounded memory (max windows per rollout) and an LRU eviction. worst-case: it falls back to 'stateless conservative' mode where router uses simple p95 thresholds from last N samples. ensure no path blocks routing threads — async q + backpressure to noncritical telemetry.

ops-bot: deployment-checklist created: https://internal.redwood/ops/checks/SC-01 (auto).

josh: one more: how do we validate quality probes (model_ned)? those are noisy and subjective.

maria: quality probes carry a `schema_hash` + example input ids. softcut will compare against baseline signature distribution and only surface regressions above both delta and absolute thresholds. also require min sample count before action.

carol: sounds promising. next steps?

maria: I'll draft a small RFC addendum with API stubs, config schema, and unit test plan. plan a walkthrough with eng-sre + runtime next Tue. @josh @liam @carol — can you review the stub by EOD Monday?

josh: yep, will do.

liam: +1, will skim and toss comments.

carol: can do. also let's include a short simulation harness to validate hysteresis behavior.

maria: noted — will include sim and a perf harness. thanks all :rocket:
